items.name: admin-theme
items.title: Admin theme
items.description: Admin colors and radii, including a pair of success and warning tokens on top of the standard shadcn set, for both light and dark schemes. Installed first: the rest of the admin-kit items rely on these tokens.

items.name: admin-shell
items.title: Admin shell
items.description: The admin's permanent frame at full viewport height: an optional header, a side navigation, and a work area with its own scroll — the sidebar and its footer stay put while the content scrolls. Navigation lives in one place per width, never two: on a wide screen it is the sidebar, on a narrow one the sidebar is gone and the burger panel carries every section with its label and the sidebarFooter. The brand and the account are not repeated inside that panel — on a narrow screen they sit on the top bar, the logo and app name on the left and sidebarProfile on the right. That is why a phone gets the full width for the work area instead of a strip of unlabelled icons duplicating a panel. The controlled collapsed prop shrinks the sidebar to a rail of icons on a wide screen; the consumer holds the state, and the sidebar toggle that expands it again is right there in the footer, so no burger appears next to it. Every row of the sidebar shares one grid: the logo, the account avatar and the nav icons all sit in the same 24px box, and its centre stays on the same vertical line whether the sidebar is expanded or collapsed. The sidebar is drawn as a card — a separate panel with rounding and inset. The header prop turns the header off entirely, and then a narrow screen gets that same compact top bar. An optional logo slot renders before appName on the brand row and stays visible in the icon rail once the name itself is hidden. Directly under the brand row, sidebarProfile renders a full-width account row separated from the navigation by a divider — the recommended home for user-menu's variant="row", because an icon in a corner reads as decoration rather than as who is signed in; in the icon rail it collapses to the trigger's avatar. sidebarActions still sits next to the app name for anything else that belongs at the top, such as a notifications button, and joins the account on the narrow top bar; sidebarFooter lives at the bottom of the sidebar and in the burger panel, and the shell — not the content — controls its layout. Nav items support icons and swapping the link render for your own router; an item without an icon shows the first letter of its title when collapsed, and the accessible name stays the section title. The burger panel remounts on every open, so slot content must be controlled from the outside — the same rule the whole kit lives by. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: theme-toggle
items.title: Theme toggle
items.description: A theme-switch button with no knowledge of how the theme is stored: the isDark state and the onToggle handler arrive as props, and there's neither next-themes nor a context of its own inside. The icon shows the state a click will switch to, and the screen-reader label changes along with it. Fits both the shell's sidebarFooter slot and a standalone spot on a page. The button carries a tooltip with the same text as its accessible name, so an icon-only control in a collapsed sidebar still says what it does.

items.name: sidebar-toggle
items.title: Sidebar toggle
items.description: A button that collapses the shell's sidebar into an icon rail on a wide screen, built like theme-toggle: the collapsed state and the onToggle handler arrive as props, with no state of its own. The icon shows the action a click will perform, and the screen-reader label changes along with it. Hidden on a narrow screen right inside the element itself — there the sidebar is already an icon rail with a burger, so the button isn't needed. Its place is the shell's sidebarFooter slot next to the theme toggle; no dedicated prop for it is needed in admin-shell. The button carries a tooltip with the same text as its accessible name, so an icon-only control in a collapsed sidebar still says what it does.

items.name: language-toggle
items.title: Language toggle
items.description: A locale-switch button with no knowledge of where the locale is stored, built like theme-toggle: the current locale, the list of available locales, and the onLocaleChange handler arrive as props, with no i18n library and no context of its own inside. The button shows the short label of the current locale (e.g. "EN"), falling back to a Languages icon before the current locale is known, and a click cycles to the next locale in the list, wrapping back to the first. Fits the shell's sidebarFooter slot next to theme-toggle or anywhere else on the page — it holds no internal state, so it renders identically in every sidebarFooter instance. The button carries a tooltip with the same text as its accessible name, so an icon-only control in a collapsed sidebar still says what it does.

items.name: user-menu
items.title: User menu
items.description: An avatar button opening a dropdown with the user's name, email, and a list of items (icon, label, and a danger tone for actions like sign-out). The avatar is the same fixed-size circle in both variants, falling back to a person icon when avatarUrl is missing — an avatar is a picture the app uploads, and a glyph reads as a placeholder where initials read as data. variant="row" (the default is "icon") fills admin-shell's sidebarProfile slot: avatar, name, the email in muted text beneath it and a trailing chevron, the whole row a single trigger — aria-labelledby points at the name and the email, so a screen reader announces who is signed in rather than a generic label, and it keeps announcing it in the collapsed rail, where that text is hidden but still counts as a referenced label. A long name or email truncates instead of widening the sidebar. variant="icon" stays the fit for sidebarActions, the header's actions slot or sidebarFooter. The trigger carries data-slot="user-menu" — the seam admin-shell restyles to collapse the row into the icon rail, and the reason not to look for data-slot="button" there, which the dropdown primitive overwrites. The dropdown's open state lives in the primitive, the same as the kit's other popups.

items.name: breadcrumbs
items.title: Breadcrumbs
items.description: A trail of section links above a page's heading. Every entry except the last renders as a link when it has an href (through renderLink when provided, a plain <a> otherwise — the same substitution pattern as admin-shell's renderLink); an entry without an href in the middle of the trail renders as plain text. The last entry is always the current page — BreadcrumbPage with aria-current="page", never a link, regardless of whether it has an href. Server-compatible: no client state, no "use client".

items.name: locale-ru
items.title: Russian locale pack
items.description: A Russian dictionary for the kit's items: a single const, localeRu, sliced into the exact shapes the other items' labels and locale props expect, so a slice spreads or passes straight into a prop — labels={localeRu.widgetTable}, locale={localeRu.dateField.locale}. Covers widget-table, widget-list, widget-chart, widget-activity, widget-donut, widget-progress, state-loading, state-error, state-forbidden, state-offline, widget-placeholder, confirm-dialog, date-field, date-time-field, date-range-field, color-field, file-field, image-field, tags-field, sidebar-toggle, theme-toggle, admin-shell, language-toggle, user-menu, and breadcrumbs, and bundles date-fns's ru locale for the date fields and widget-activity. The dateRangeField slice reuses date-range-field's default presets' ids and range math and only swaps in Russian labels, so the two never drift apart. Not a runtime i18n solution — it's a static dictionary, and switching locale at runtime is on the consumer.

items.name: widget-metric
items.title: Metric widget
items.description: A single-number card for a dashboard: title, value, an optional trend with an arrow, and a caption. direction sets the arrow, and a separate tone prop sets the color (derived from direction by default). trendValues, given two or more points, draws a small line chart under the caption — leave it out and the card renders byte-identical to before. Data is passed as props. Requires the admin-theme theme. Hovering the sparkline shows the exact point value, formatted via trendTooltipFormat. loading swaps the value, trend and sparkline for skeleton bars while the title stays put.

items.name: widget-table
items.title: Table widget
items.description: A self-sufficient table card: the title is optional, the header holds a toolbar slot for filters on the left and a record count, page-size select and sort select on the right, and the footer holds centered pagination. A column pulls its value from the row via cell and aligns with the align prop; a column with sortable gets a sort button in its header and aria-sort. The sort select is set with a sortOptions list, and an option's key need not match a column: that allows sorting by a field which is not rendered, or applying a composite sort behind one opaque key. Sorting and paging are controlled: the table reports the choice via onSortChange and onPageChange but never reorders or slices the rows itself — whoever owns the data sets the order and the slice, otherwise the item would lie on a server with paginated output. With no rows and no empty prop of its own it shows state-empty, and the header and footer stay in place. Passing both selectedKeys and onSelectionChange adds a checkbox column: the header checkbox selects or clears the current page only, and once a row is selected the header's left side becomes a selection bar with an N-selected count, the selectionActions as icon buttons the size of row actions (an action without an icon keeps its text label) and a clear button — every icon-only control there carries a tooltip and an aria-label taken from the same string. When totalCount exceeds the selected count and the whole page is selected, onSelectAllMatching adds a button offering to extend the selection to every matching record, worded by selectAllMatchingLabel; the table never computes that selection itself, since only the data owner behind the filter knows the keys. loading swaps the rows for skeleton bars in the same column layout and withholds the sort select, pagination and selection bar until the data arrives. filtered switches the default empty state for a filtered-results one, with its own title and description and, when onClearFilters is given, a clear-filters button — "nothing matches this filter" and "there is nothing here yet" call for different words and different actions. hiddenColumnIds hides columns, and once onHiddenColumnIdsChange is set the header gets a columns icon button (columnsLabel) dropping down the column checkboxes; a column marked alwaysVisible shows there checked and disabled, and a column with an empty title — an actions column has no name to show and no business being hidden — does not appear at all. stickyHeader keeps the header row in view while the body scrolls inside its own focusable, labelled scroll area sized by maxBodyHeight (24rem by default). It always owns that scroll area on purpose: sticking to whatever scroller the page provides cannot be made correct once that scroller has padding of its own, because a row keeps showing above the stuck header in the padding strip. The exported toCsv helper turns columns and rows into an RFC 4180 string, but the table renders no export control of its own — export is one more selectionAction the consumer wires up, usually calling toCsv on the selected rows.

items.name: widget-chart
items.title: Chart widget
items.description: A chart card for a dashboard: a shared labels axis and a series list, each with its own values — the values length must match labels, or the missing points simply aren't drawn. The kind prop switches the rendering between a line (default) and bars. Series color comes from the chart-1…chart-5 tokens in order; past five series the colors cycle, and two series of the same color on one chart read as a bug. The legend appears only when there's more than one series. With no labels or no series at all it shows the "No data" state. Requires the admin-theme theme. The header has a toolbar slot on the right — a period picker like date-range-field drops straight in. loading swaps the chart for a skeleton block of the same height, checked ahead of the empty state.

items.name: widget-list
items.title: List widget
items.description: A list of rows for a dashboard: a title, an optional description under it, an optional meta on the right, and an optional icon on the left. The icon is accepted as a component — the element doesn't pull in a specific icon library. With no rows and no empty prop passed it shows StateEmpty with "No data". Requires the admin-theme theme. loading swaps the rows for skeleton bars at the same row rhythm, checked ahead of the empty state.

items.name: widget-placeholder
items.title: Widget placeholder
items.description: A dashed frame with muted text marking a spot in the work area where a widget hasn't been chosen yet. It doesn't show a "no data" state — widgets already have a built-in StateEmpty for that; this placeholder is about the widget itself being missing, not about data being missing inside it. Both texts are optional and default to English. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-loading
items.title: Loading state
items.description: A skeleton in place of content while data is on its way. The row count is set by a prop, and role=status and aria-busy are set for screen readers. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-empty
items.title: Empty state
items.description: The screen a user sees in place of content when there's no data: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot. No data is normal, so there's no icon by default. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-error
items.title: Error state
items.description: A screen for a loading or request failure: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with an error icon by default — the failure should read before the text does. Not for missing data — state-empty covers that. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-forbidden
items.title: Forbidden state
items.description: A screen for access denial: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with a muted lock icon by default — lacking permissions is a denial, not a breakage, so the color isn't alarming. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: state-offline
items.title: Offline state
items.description: A screen for a lost connection: a title, an optional description, and an optional actions slot, with a network-disconnect icon by default — the failure should read before the text does. Not for a server error — state-error covers that. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: page-entity
items.title: Entity page
items.description: A single-record page: a title with actions on the right and fields grouped into sections. A section lays its fields out in two columns by default; the columns prop takes 1, 2 or 3, and three columns is what keeps a record of short values from spreading over a screen of empty space. A field's value is a ReactNode, not a string: links, badges, and amounts with their own formatting live alongside the text. A section without a title is allowed — for an unnamed header made of the main fields. The status prop swaps the fields for one of the loading, error, forbidden, or offline states, while the title stays visible. No forms, no editing: edit buttons live in actions. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: page-header
items.title: Section header
items.description: A page title, an optional description under it, and an actions slot on the right. A building block for every admin page, not a dashboard widget. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: status-badge
items.title: Status badge
items.description: A record-status badge: an order is new or cancelled, a product is in stock or out, a user is active or blocked. The tone is set by the tone prop (neutral, success, warning, danger) rather than derived from the text. The success and warning colors come from the admin-kit theme's tokens of the same name — the standard shadcn set doesn't have them, so the element requires the admin-theme theme and colors incorrectly without it. A building block for a page, not a dashboard widget.

items.name: admin-toaster
items.title: Toast notifications
items.description: Toasts about an operation's outcome: an order was saved, an email failed to send, stock is running low. AdminToaster is placed once — in the root layout or in the shell — and shows nothing by itself; toasts are triggered by calling notify.info, notify.success, notify.warning, and notify.danger from anywhere in the code, including handlers outside React. The element has no state or context of its own: the queue lives in the toast primitive's manager. The tone sets the whole toast's color — the same tokens as status-badge: neutral dark for info, success, warning, and destructive for the rest — and its icon; optional description and an actionLabel/onAction pair add explanatory text and an action button inside the toast.

items.name: confirm-dialog
items.title: Confirm dialog
items.description: A confirmation dialog for an action — delete a record, cancel an order, revoke access. Controlled: the consumer holds open and onOpenChange, and closing it after success is on them too, so the dialog can be left open while a request is still in flight. The tone prop colors the confirm button (default, or danger for an irreversible action), and loading disables both buttons, shows a busy indicator, and blocks closing via Escape or an outside click. Button labels are set by props, defaulting to "Confirm" and "Cancel".

items.name: form-dialog
items.title: Form dialog
items.description: A modal with a real form for quick edits: a title, an optional description, consumer-laid-out fields as children, and a footer with Cancel and Save. Save submits the form element, submitting disables both buttons, sets aria-busy and blocks closing by Escape or an outside click while the operation is in progress — the same guard confirm-dialog uses. Controlled: the consumer holds open, onOpenChange and the field state; submitLabel and cancelLabel localize the buttons. For a full create/edit page use page-form instead.

items.name: hint
items.title: Hint
items.description: A tooltip hint for a field label, column header, or metric: it explains a term or what goes into a figure, without taking up screen space. With no children it draws a muted question-mark icon whose accessible name comes from text; with children it wraps the passed element with its own trigger and draws no icon. The side prop picks which side it pops up on, and the render prop swaps in your own element instead of the default trigger — this lets you hang the hint on an existing button instead of nesting a button inside a button. The trigger is a native button, so the hint also opens from the keyboard; TooltipProvider isn't required, it only syncs the delay between neighboring tooltips.

items.name: row-actions
items.title: Row actions
items.description: A row of compact icon buttons for a table row or a list card: view, edit, delete. The label takes up no space in the row but remains the button's accessible name and pops up as a tooltip on hover — the element reuses hint for that. The danger tone colors the icon with the destructive color, and disabled blocks an individual action. Controlled: each action gets its own onSelect, and the element holds no state of its own.

items.name: date-field
items.title: Date field
items.description: A single-date picker with a calendar in a popover. The value is a YYYY-MM-DD string, and an empty string means "nothing selected": there's no Date object and no timezone in the props — parsing and formatting go by local date components, so the value never drifts a day off during serialization or on the server. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange. The trigger button, as wide as the field, shows the date in English (e.g. "August 10, 2026"), and picking a date in the calendar closes the popover right away. The label prop draws a caption and links it to the trigger.

items.name: date-time-field
items.title: Date-time field
items.description: A picker for a date together with a time. The value is a YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm string with no seconds and no timezone, and an empty string means "nothing selected". Controlled, built like date-field but deliberately independent of it: registry items are installed one at a time, so each one parses its string on its own. The popover has a time field next to the calendar — changing the date keeps the chosen time, changing the time keeps the date, and if there's no date yet, today is used. The popover doesn't close when a date is picked, or there'd be no time to set the time.

items.name: date-range-field
items.title: Date range field
items.description: A range picker: a trigger button showing the two dates joined by an en dash, and a popover with a preset column on the left and a two-month range calendar on the right. The value is a single YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD string — the ".." separator keeps a range a single PageListFilter-compatible string — and an empty string means "nothing selected"; parsing is calendar-strict like date-field and rejects a from later than to. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange. Presets (Today, Yesterday, This week, This month, This year, Last week, Last month, Last year by default, overridable via the presets prop) compute their range from an explicit today argument, so "this week" and the rest stay deterministic in tests; weeks start on Monday regardless of locale, matching the calendar primitive. Clicking a preset commits and closes the popover immediately; picking a range on the calendar commits only once both ends are chosen — a lone start date stays inside the popup and never reaches onChange. page-list wires this in as its date-range filter kind. A range can also be selected in one gesture — press a day and drag across the calendar with the mouse or a finger; two separate clicks with a live hover preview work as well, and a lone start date stays inside the popover's own state. width works like select-field's: "auto" by default, "full" to pin the trigger to its container.

items.name: time-field
items.title: Time field
items.description: A time picker built on a native input type=time: the value is an HH:mm string in 24-hour format, and an empty string means "nothing selected". Controlled, holds no state of its own. The step prop sets the step in minutes (5 by default) and is converted to seconds internally, as the native element requires; min and max constrain the selection in the same format. The native base is a deliberate choice — it gives keyboard input, a local format, and a mobile picker with no code of your own; the clock icon is inverted in the dark theme.

items.name: color-field
items.title: Color field
items.description: A color picker for entities that carry their own color — an order tag, a product category, a kanban column. The value is a HEX string like #rrggbb, and an empty string means "nothing selected"; the color always leaves the component in lowercase. Controlled. Inside the popover: a grid of quick colors from presets (its own palette of twelve data colors, not theme tokens — otherwise the value stored in the consumer's database would shift along with the look), a native input type=color for an arbitrary shade, and a text field for manually typing a HEX code, where an unfinished entry never leaves as a value.

items.name: text-field
items.title: Text field
items.description: A single-line text input. The value is a string; the type prop switches between text, email, password, url and tel. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: number-field
items.title: Number field
items.description: A numeric input. The value is deliberately a string and passes through unparsed — mid-typing states like "1." or "-" cannot live in a number, and the kit's field values stay serializable; the consumer parses on submit. min, max and step forward to the native input. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: textarea-field
items.title: Textarea field
items.description: A multi-line text input with a rows prop (4 by default). The value is a string. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: select-field
items.title: Select field
items.description: A single-choice select over an options list of value/label pairs. An empty value shows the placeholder ("Select…" by default — the placeholder prop localizes it); the popup is pinned to the trigger like the kit's other selects. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange. width picks how wide the trigger is: "auto" (the default) lets it size to its content in a toolbar and stretch in a column form, "full" pins it to the container.

items.name: checkbox-field
items.title: Checkbox field
items.description: A boolean checkbox with its label to the right; hint or error render below the pair. Controlled via checked and onChange. Renders label, control, hint and error in the kit's shared field anatomy: when error is set it replaces the hint, the control gets aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Controlled: the consumer holds value and onChange.

items.name: file-field
items.title: File field
items.description: A file picker built like the kit's other fields — label, hint, error — with one deliberate exception: value is File | null and onChange takes a File | null, not a string. A File can't be serialized into a string the way every other field's value is, and faking it with an object URL would leak the reference; checkbox-field's boolean is the kit's other exception to the string convention. accept restricts the file type the same way the native attribute does. The drop zone accepts a dragged file and highlights on dragover, buttonLabel opens the native picker, and the selected name and size (formatFileSize, exported and tested for B/KB/MB) show next to it, or noFileLabel when nothing's chosen; a ghost X button clears the selection. The native input stays in the DOM, visually hidden rather than display:none, so Tab and Enter/Space still reach and drive it. A disabled field is marked aria-disabled, so the dimmed text reads as inactive rather than as low-contrast content. The container is positioned, so the visually hidden native input cannot stretch the page and add a second scrollbar on a long form.

items.name: image-field
items.title: Image field
items.description: A gallery field for a record's images: thumbnails in a responsive grid, a drop zone that takes dragged files or opens the native picker, reordering by drag, a full-size preview in a dialog, a direct link that opens the original in a new tab, and removal that applies straight away — the field has no Apply button of its own, because a form's Save is the only one there should be. Like every item in the kit it never uploads anything: onSelect hands the picked File objects to the consumer, which stores them and returns the result through value as {id, url, name} items, so the same field works over S3, a REST endpoint or an object URL. onChange reports the new order and the removals. multiple=false narrows it to a single image and maxItems caps the set, hiding the drop zone once it is full; limitImageFieldFiles (exported and tested) is what drops non-images and trims a selection to that cap. Reordering works without a mouse: every thumbnail carries move-earlier and move-later buttons alongside preview, open and remove, since HTML5 drag is unreachable from a keyboard; moveImageFieldItem is exported for the same move applied outside the field. Labels are props with English defaults, and each thumbnail's controls name the image they act on. Requires the admin-theme theme.

items.name: tags-field
items.title: Tags field
items.description: A multi-value tag input: value is a string array and onChange replaces it wholesale, the same convention as every other controlled field. Enter or a comma commits the trimmed input as a new tag, ignoring an empty or duplicate one (case-sensitive as typed); Backspace on an empty input drops the last tag. Each tag renders as a Badge with its own X to remove it — removeLabel sets that button's aria-label, defaulting to `Remove ${tag}`. suggestions, when given, filters to matches as you type, excludes tags already added, and lists them in a small popup under the input. Exports addTag(tags, raw), the pure commit logic, for testing or reuse.

items.name: page-form
items.title: Form page
items.description: A create/edit record page: a header with a title, description and an actions slot, sections of consumer-laid-out fields (a section's columns prop takes 2 or 3 and turns the section into a responsive grid where each field is one cell, so a form of a dozen short fields stops being one tall column; a field that needs the full width says so with col-span), and a footer with Cancel and Save (labels are props, so they localize). It is a real form element — Save submits, submitting disables both buttons and sets aria-busy. The status prop (ready/loading/error/forbidden/offline) swaps the sections for the matching State screen while the header stays. Requires the state screens it renders.

items.name: widget-progress
items.title: Progress widget
items.description: A progress-bar card for a dashboard: warehouse fill level, plan completion, quota usage. Next to the bar is a percentage share computed against max (100 by default). A value outside the range doesn't break the layout: a negative one counts as zero, one above max counts as the maximum. An optional target draws a tick mark on the bar at target/max and a right-aligned targetLabel caption ("Goal" by default) — target is clamped into [0, max] the same way value is. Requires the admin-theme theme. The tone prop recolors the bar (default/success/warning/danger theme tokens) so a goal that is behind schedule reads at a glance; the consumer decides the thresholds. loading swaps the bar and the percentage for skeleton bars while the title stays put. The bar takes its accessible name from title, so a screen reader announces which target is at 62% rather than an anonymous progress bar.

items.name: widget-activity
items.title: Activity widget
items.description: A recent-activity feed card for a dashboard: entries carry a title, an optional secondary meta line, an optional icon, and a YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm timestamp — the same string family date-time-field uses, parsed the same strict way. Entries are grouped by calendar day; the group header reads labels.today or labels.yesterday relative to the actual current date, and dayFormat (a date-fns pattern) for anything older. Within a group, entries keep the order they're given — the item never resorts them. With no entries it shows state-empty. Requires the admin-theme theme. loading swaps the entries for skeleton rows at the same rhythm, checked ahead of the empty state. Entries are laid out in one left-hand column — time, icon, then title and meta — so nothing drifts to the far edge on a wide card, and the day heading sits above that same column. dayFormat controls the heading, which matters outside English: a Russian locale needs "d MMMM", not the English "MMMM d".

items.name: widget-donut
items.title: Donut widget
items.description: A donut-chart card for a dashboard: a list of labeled slices, each drawn as a ring segment and as a row in the legend beside it — a color dot, the label, and valueFormat(value, share) right-aligned, where share is value divided by the total (the default renders it as a rounded percentage). Colors cycle through the chart-1…chart-5 tokens in order. With no slices, or slices that total zero, it shows state-empty. Requires the admin-theme theme. loading swaps the ring and the legend for skeleton shapes of the same size, checked ahead of the empty state.

items.name: widget-quick-actions
items.title: Quick actions widget
items.description: A grid of shortcut buttons for a dashboard: id, label, an optional icon component, and an onSelect handler per action. columns switches the grid between two (default) and three columns. With no actions it renders the titled card with an empty grid — that's a consumer mistake, not a data state, so it doesn't fall back to state-empty. Requires the admin-theme theme. loading swaps the action buttons for skeleton blocks in the same grid, so nothing is clickable mid-fetch.

items.name: page-list
items.title: List page
items.description: A list page: a section title, optional actions, a filter bar, a table, and pagination underneath it. Everything is controlled: the page stores neither the current page number nor the filter values, it receives them as props and reports changes via onFilterChange and onPageChange. The status prop picks the body's content: loading, error, forbidden, and offline swap in the matching state, ready shows the table; the title and filters stay visible under any status, so the request can be retried with a different filter. Pagination is built from page, pageSize, and total, and isn't rendered at all if total isn't passed. A filter is a text search, a dropdown list, or a date-range picker (rendered via date-range-field, its value passed through as-is and reported the same way as the other kinds). Row selection forwards straight through to widget-table, the same way sorting and pagination do: pass selectedKeys, onSelectionChange, and selectionActions and the underlying table renders the checkbox column and selection bar. Requires the admin-theme theme. filtered, onClearFilters, hiddenColumnIds, onHiddenColumnIdsChange and onExport forward straight through to widget-table: the page decides what counts as filtered and what to export, the table only renders the resulting state and controls. onResetFilters, labelled by resetFiltersLabel (default "Reset filters"), adds an icon button at the end of the filter bar; it appears only once the callback is given and at least one filter holds a non-empty value, and its tooltip and accessible name are the same string. It answers a different question than the table's onClearFilters — "a filter control holds a value" rather than "the query narrowed the rows to zero" — so the two stay separate props, though a consumer usually points both at one handler. A select filter must model its unset state as an empty value with no matching option: a catch-all sentinel like "all" counts as a value and would keep the reset button on screen forever.

items.name: combobox-field
items.title: Combobox field
items.description: A single-select field with type-ahead search over a value/label options list, for picking one record out of hundreds — a customer, a product, a warehouse — where select-field's plain dropdown stops scaling. The visible input shows the selected option's label when closed and the typed query while searching; filterComboboxOptions matches the trimmed query as a case-insensitive substring anywhere in the label, and is exported and unit-tested on its own. Clearing the field always calls onChange(""), so the field never holds a selection the parent doesn't know about. When any option carries a group, matching options render under their group's name and ungrouped options keep their original order ahead of the named groups; with no groups at all the list is flat. emptyLabel ("Nothing found" by default) renders when a query matches nothing, placeholder ("Search…") sits in the empty input. Keyboard movement, Enter and Escape come from the underlying Base UI combobox rather than hand-rolled key handling, so Enter does not submit an enclosing form while the popup is open. Shares the label/hint/error anatomy of every other field: error replaces hint and sets aria-invalid. The trigger and the clear button carry accessible names of their own (openLabel, clearLabel), since an icon-only button is silent to a screen reader otherwise.

items.name: page-auth
items.title: Auth page
items.description: The sign-in screen, and the one common admin screen that lives outside the shell: a centered card on an empty full-height page, with no header, sidebar or navigation. appName sits above the card title — the only place the product names itself here. The item ships no email or password field of its own, because which fields a sign-in needs (email, phone, one-time code, tenant picker) differs per project and the kit already has fields for all of them: they go in as children. The card body is a real form and onSubmit receives the raw submit event — the item never calls preventDefault for you. submitLabel defaults to "Sign in" on a full-width button; while submitting is true that button and every field inside are disabled together through a wrapping fieldset, so a second submit cannot race the first, and the form is marked aria-busy. error renders above the button as an assertive role=alert live region, so a failed sign-in reaches a screen reader. footer sits under the card for a forgot-password or sign-up link. aside, when given, renders a second panel beside the card from the lg breakpoint up — the illustration half of a split sign-in screen — and is hidden below it, leaving the card simply centered.

items.name: multi-select-field
items.title: Multi-select field
items.description: Pick several options out of a fixed list of value/label pairs — the counterpart to tags-field, which takes free text instead. value is a string array and onChange replaces it wholesale, the same convention as every other controlled field. Built on the Base UI combobox in chips mode: the chosen options sit as removable chips inside the input, typing filters the list case-insensitively, and already-selected options stay listed and marked so they can be unselected. Backspace on an empty input drops the last chip; each chip's remove button gets its aria-label from removeLabel, which takes the option's label and defaults to `Remove ${label}`. maxItems, when set, disables the options beyond the limit rather than hiding them, so it is visible why nothing happens — selected options stay clickable and the search keeps working. emptyLabel ("Nothing found") shows when a query matches nothing; placeholder ("Search…") only shows while nothing is selected. Enter never submits a surrounding form. Exports toggleMultiSelectValue(value, option), the pure add/remove logic that also drives the component, for testing or reuse.

items.name: page-tabs
items.title: Page tabs
items.description: Section navigation inside a single page — the tabs that split an order or customer screen into Overview, History and Settings without navigating away. Controlled like every item in the kit: value and onValueChange come from props, so the active tab can be routed through a URL query string; the item stores nothing itself. Only the active panel's content mounts — the underlying Base UI panel defaults to keepMounted false and unmounts a hidden panel's subtree instead of hiding it, so a heavy table on a hidden tab never renders while another tab is open. Each item's icon renders before the label and badge after it (a count or a status dot); disabled disables a trigger without removing it from the strip. actions renders on the same row as the tab strip, pushed to the far end, for a page-level button that belongs beside the tabs rather than inside a panel — on a narrow screen the row wraps instead of pushing the actions off screen, and the strip itself scrolls horizontally when the labels do not fit. Keyboard movement and ARIA (role=tablist, arrow keys, aria-selected) come from the primitive rather than being hand-rolled.
